summary: Submitted draft/submission.json (action=research) with the map update draft/map-v7.json as the new base (base version 6): a consolidation step after the sixth obligation was answered in scope. The candidate behavior's remaining question was two questions in one, and the second half is now answered — with the two-leader overlap of one term in place and the two leaders kept apart, one leader committed a client write at an index where the only other reachable voter already held a different entry with the same index and term, so two leaders of one term can commit conflicting entries — so that half is removed from the frontier and the question is narrowed to whether the dual leadership can be made to persist. The follower behavior now records the mechanism the consequence turns on, namely that the conflict loop compares terms only: an entry whose index and term already match is not written and success is reported, so the acknowledgement the leader counts asserts the position rather than the contents, together with the protection that bounds it, namely that log matching follows from the vote rule wherever one leader exists per term. The core overview rationale now says that with the dual leadership in place the commit line inherits that consequence and that only the persistence question remains, so the summary matches the current understanding while the status stays usable and no core gap is claimed. The submission carries three clarification map_changes and states explicitly that no requirement, identity, context or fact edge changed: the behaviors keep their owners, triggers, guards, reads, writes, produced and consumed facts and sources, and only one branch statement, one protection statement, one narrowed question and the overview sentence were touched. It also carries a handoff feedback that cites the two relevant check runs (the overlap and the committed-entry check), records the answered half in its own words, and lists the four remaining leads: whether the dual leadership can be made to persist, whether production TCP scheduling reproduces the heartbeat interleaving, whether the client-future non-completion also occurs for a request enqueued before Shutdown and which repair is intended, and the deferred surface about the commit context a follower leaves after installing a snapshot. One small mechanical correction was needed before submission: an extraneous field was removed from the feedback object so it matches the research-feedback shape. Optional preflight with the trusted validator returned valid=true; no target code was executed for this product, and the run now stands at six confirmed in-scope findings with three consensus-safety results among them.
